title: Where Love Becomes Light
author: Madhusudan Mishra
text:
Before your voice entered my days, The sky was beautiful, yet
incomplete; Then every sunset found a deeper hue, and silence
learned a gentler heartbeat.
You came like rain on thirsty earth, A blessing neither sought nor
planned; The seasons gathered in your smile, and bloomed like
gardens at your hand.
Love is not the fire that fades, nor fleeting sparks that briefly
shine; It is the moon upon dark waters, Turning ordinary moments
divine.
I find your presence in the wind, that wanders softly through the
trees; A hidden music fills the air, Composed in notes of memory.
Though oceans stretch between our shores, no distance alters
what is true; The stars may travel countless years, yet still their
light arrives anew.
Your kindness leaves a trail of dawn, Across the landscapes of the
heart; A quiet grace that teaches hope, and keeps all shadows far
apart.
If time should write its silver lines Upon the pages of our days,
my soul would still recognize yours, Beyond the reach of age or
change.
And when the final evening falls, and earthly songs grow faint
and few, Love will remain—a timeless light, forever finding its
way to you.
